expectations.evidence: "Endpoint: POST /api/auth/login (public)" explicitly stated in Phase 2 (Login), and also shown in the summary diagram as "POST /auth/login → AuthController ..."

expectations.text: Mentions JWT token generation (JwtService or equivalent)
expectations.evidence: "JwtService.generateToken(userDetails)" is shown in the backend login chain, and the key file "onlineshopapi/.../security/JwtService.java" is listed. The summary diagram also shows "JwtService.generateToken() (HMAC-SHA, 24h)".

expectations.text: Mentions localStorage as where the token is stored on the frontend
expectations.evidence: "Calls persistToken(): sets the token signal and writes to localStorage under key access_token" in Phase 2 frontend chain. Also: "AuthService constructor reads localStorage.getItem('access_token') into the token signal synchronously" in Phase 3.

expectations.text: Mentions AuthTokenInterceptor as the mechanism that attaches the Bearer header
expectations.evidence: Phase 4 is titled "Attaching the token to every subsequent request" and states: "authTokenInterceptor (features/auth/interceptors/auth-token.interceptor.ts): ... If a token exists, clones the request and adds Authorization: Bearer <token>."

expectations.text: Mentions JwtAuthFilter as the backend token validation component
expectations.evidence: Phase 5 is titled "Per-request validation on the backend" and opens with "JwtAuthFilter (security/JwtAuthFilter.java, extends OncePerRequestFilter): Runs before UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter on every request..."

expectations.text: Mentions user roles (ADMIN and CUSTOMER) and @PreAuthorize for method-level enforcement
expectations.evidence: "Method-level: @PreAuthorize(\"hasRole('ADMIN')\") on write operations in ProductController and ProductCategoryController." Also: registration forces "role to CUSTOMER", and rolesGuard uses "roles: ['ADMIN']".

expectations.text: Mentions Angular guards (authGuard and/or rolesGuard) for route protection
expectations.evidence: The "Frontend route protection" section explicitly lists all three guards in a table: authGuard, guestGuard, and rolesGuard, with their checks and redirect behaviors.
